According to Reuters, the 67 include the 19 from the two Arab-led parties, which Eisenkot for now does not want in government. Al Jazeera reports that he says he is open to a government with Netanyahu and Smotrich if Likud and Religious Zionism support it. According to the Times of Israel, three Jewish opposition parties have so far refused to ally with Arab parties, and it is unclear whether United Torah Judaism will enter the government: it rejects compulsory national service for all, a principle of Eisenkot's.

Transport Secretary Sean Duffy thanked controllers and passengers and said that operations have returned to full capacity, Ansa reports on 14 November. Reuters writes that the shutdown, of almost five hours, was attributed to a router installed by L3Harris, and that over 20,000 flights have suffered disruptions since Friday; according to the head of the FAA, cited by Reuters, a return to normal for flights is not expected before Sunday evening.

On Friday 13 November the FAA, the American civil aviation authority, blocked all take-offs in the United States for «extraordinary circumstances and safety reasons», writes Al Jazeera. The shutdown began at 15:54 in New York (21:54 in Italy) and was lifted in the evening: Transport Secretary Sean Duffy indicated the reopening of airspace at 20:15 in New York, that is 1:15 on Saturday in Italy. Open and Il Post speak of about four hours, Al Jazeera of five.

The cause indicated is a telecommunications outage that involved en-route air traffic control centres, according to Al Jazeera. Duffy explained that switches and routers overloaded with data went haywire, without a total loss of communications or radar. Homeland Security Secretary Mullin said that there is no cyberattack nor a danger to the public, and that it is not «a new 9/11», but according to Ansa he also said that nothing can be ruled out regarding the causes. The FBI rules out a cyberattack or a crime, Ansa reports. Microsoft said it has no indication of a link to its Outlook service disruption, according to the same agency.

The numbers differ according to the source. According to FlightRadar24, cited by Al Jazeera, the flights cancelled on Friday are more than 4,700 and delays are about 10,000, with another 700 flights already cancelled for Saturday. The monthly net minimum wage rises from 1,477.93 to 1,502 euros. The automatic revaluation was scheduled for January.

The Data Protection Authority has fined Meta €805 million, report Open and Il Post. According to Open, the penalty is worth approximately 0.47% of the group's global turnover. The Authority challenges the Facebook app for Android regarding access to photos, videos and metadata on users' phones without specific consent and without adequate information; Open writes that approximately 20 million Android users in Italy are affected.

Meta says it disagrees, defines the fine as disproportionate and maintains that the feature requires a permission that can be modified at any time; the company announces an appeal, reports Open.
